rules.source: Ley de Protección de los Datos Personales, Ley 25.326 — https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/ley-25326-64790/texto
rules.retrieved_snippet: Objective: comprehensive protection of personal data recorded in files/registers/databases, public or private, to guarantee the right to honor and privacy and access to one's own recorded information. Sanctioned 2000-10-04, published in Boletín Oficial 2000-11-02.

rules.source: Argentina.gob.ar — Protección de datos y privacidad de niños, niñas y adolescentes en entornos digitales — https://www.argentina.gob.ar/noticias/proteccion-de-datos-y-privacidad-de-ninos-ninas-y-adolescentes-en-entornos-digitales
rules.retrieved_snippet: Under Ley 25.326 and the Civil and Commercial Code (arts. 26, 639, 'progressive autonomy' principle from the CRC): consent of persons 16+ is valid; for younger children, treatment is lawful only with consent from whoever exercises parental responsibility.
The Civil and Commercial Code considers minors persons under 18, adolescents from 13; the 'Con vos en la Web' government program addresses children/adolescent online protection specifically.

rules.source: Ley de Defensa del Consumidor, Ley 24.240 — https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/ley-24240-638
rules.retrieved_snippet: Establishes the rights of consumers and obligations of providers in consumption relations. Sanctioned 1993-09-22, published in Boletín Oficial 1993-10-15.

aliases: acceso ilegítimo a un sistema informático
rules.source: Ley 26.388 (2008), modificación del Código Penal — delitos informáticos — https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/ley-26388-141790/texto
rules.retrieved_snippet: Sanctioned 2008-06-04 and published in the Boletín Oficial 2008-06-25, it amends the Código Penal to criminalize computer damage, computer fraud, alteration of evidence and offenses against privacy; art. 153 bis penalizes access to a restricted-access computer system or data, with an aggravated penalty where the victim is a public body or a financial or public-service provider.

aliases: acoso sexual infantil por medios electrónicos
rules.source: Ley 26.904 (2013) — Código Penal art. 131; complemented by Ley 27.590 'Mica Ortega' (2020) and Decreto 407/2022 — https://servicios.infoleg.gob.ar/infolegInternet/verNorma.do?id=223586
rules.retrieved_snippet: Art. 131 punishes with prison of six months to four years anyone who, by electronic communications, telecommunications or other data-transmission technology, contacts a minor with the purpose of committing any offense against the minor's sexual integrity; sanctioned 2013-11-13, published 2013-12-11.

rules.source: Ley 23.592 (actos discriminatorios), as amended by Ley 25.608 — https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/ley-23592-20465/actualizacion
rules.retrieved_snippet: Art. 1: whoever arbitrarily impedes, obstructs, restricts or impairs the full exercise on equal terms of constitutional rights and guarantees must cease the act and repair moral and material damage; discriminatory motives considered include race, religion, nationality, ideology, political or union opinion, sex, economic position, social condition or physical characteristics.

Art. 3 sets prison of one month to three years for those who participate in an organization or carry out propaganda based on ideas of racial or religious superiority, or who incite hatred or persecution against persons for race, religion, nationality or political ideas; art. 2 raises the penalty scale of Penal Code offenses committed out of persecution or hatred of a race, religion or nationality.

rules.source: Ley 25.246 (encubrimiento y lavado de activos de origen delictivo), creating the Unidad de Información Financiera (UIF) — https://servicios.infoleg.gob.ar/infolegInternet/anexos/60000-64999/62977/texact.htm
rules.retrieved_snippet: Sanctioned in 2000, it modified the offense of concealment, created the UIF, set the duty of obligated subjects to report suspicious operations without delay (art. 20) and a penal sanction regime; Ley 26.268 added terrorism-financing prevention and Ley 26.683 gave the UIF supervisory powers; regulated by Decreto 290/2007.

rules.source: Ley 11.723 (Régimen Legal de la Propiedad Intelectual, 1933) — https://servicios.infoleg.gob.ar/infolegInternet/anexos/40000-44999/42755/texact.htm
rules.retrieved_snippet: Protects authors of scientific, literary, artistic or didactic works including computer programs and databases (per argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil); art. 5 in the current Infoleg text sets protection for heirs at 70 years from 1 January following the author's death and extends it to performers and phonogram producers; regulated by Decreto 41.233/1934.
